title: For a Limited Time Only
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This article applies the marketing principle of time-based scarcity to internal organizational programs, arguing that leaders can boost engagement with hard-to-fill initiatives by framing them as limited-time offers. It explains the psychological mechanism — people anticipate the loss of a scarce opportunity and act to avoid missing out — and gives examples of internal LTO messaging for surveys, wellness programs, and award nominations. The piece cautions that these offers work best when genuinely meaningful, fair, and truly time-bound, since gimmicky or artificial deadlines are taken less seriously by team members.
points: The scarcity principle from decades of marketing — limited-time offers create urgency — applies equally well inside organizations.
Research shows framing an opportunity as time-scarce increases motivation because people want to avoid the feeling of missing out.
Internal Limited Time Offers (LTOs) work well for hard-to-fill programs like surveys, wellness initiatives, and award nominations.
LTOs are most effective when genuinely meaningful, fair, and truly time-bound rather than gimmicky.
quotes: The idea of providing a service, offering a product, or giving people access to a program for a limited time period has been a mainstay of marketing for over a century.
The concept applies the principle of scarcity to create more urgency, attention, and action.
Leaders can make any program or initiative appear more attractive and important by applying the same scarcity principle.
The enrollment or nomination window imposes a concrete deadline that nudges people to step forward and act.
Any program, initiative, or service that is hard to fill or to gain compliance with is ripe for an LTO.
